children: has received its first purchase order from multinational defence group MBDA, which has commissioned the Australian industrial technology company to undertake two joint capability studies.
The $125,000 order will cover half the cost of the $250,000 study program, providing Aurora with non-dilutive funding for the next stage of its collaboration with the European defence group.
The partners will examine the feasibility of establishing manufacturing capability for Aurora’s 3D-printed turbojet engines within MBDA’s existing European facilities.

The commissioned work follows a joint technology assessment completed in March 2026 and a teaming agreement signed in May, building on a relationship that began with a non-binding agreement in December 2025.
Aurora is developing advanced propulsion systems for unmanned aerial systems in the defence sector alongside its industrial metal printing business in Western Australia.

Aurora initially responded to a request for information from MBDA in December 2025, with the Australian company’s engine technology identified as a potential candidate for a defence program, and the parties subsequently undertook a joint assessment under their memorandum of understanding to evaluate the suitability of Aurora’s propulsion systems for MBDA’s requirements.

The two new studies will address manufacturing feasibility and technical requirements, with the partners aiming to reduce program risks and inform decisions on whether to proceed with further development.

Each study comprises six weeks of jointly conducted work under the original MOU, with the remaining commercial details confidential; while the purchase order marks a transition to funded work, neither study constitutes a commitment to proceed to a subsequent program phase.

“Advancing these capability studies alongside MBDA represents a significant milestone for Aurora Labs and validates the growing strategic relevance of our 3D-printed propulsion technology within global defence programs,” chief operating officer Rebekah Letheby said.

“The potential to establish sovereign turbojet manufacturing capability within MBDA’s European facilities is particularly compelling, aligning with increasing demand across Europe for localised, resilient defence supply chains.”
MBDA is jointly owned by Airbus and BAE Systems, which each hold 37.5%, with Italian aerospace and defence group Leonardo holding the remaining 25%.
The multinational group employs approximately 20,000 people worldwide and has relationships with more than 90 armed forces, spanning land, sea and air defence markets.
Aurora’s broader industrial technology business specialises in 3D metal printing, the supply of printed industrial components and the development of printers and associated intellectual property.
“This engagement provides Aurora with a clear pathway to participate in large-scale, long-duration defence programs, supported by one of the world’s leading defence organisations,” Ms Letheby added.

“As we progress through these studies, our focus is on delivering outcomes that support advancement into concept design and demonstration phases, while continuing to position Aurora as a key technology partner in the evolving global defence landscape.”

title: Aurora Labs Receives First Order for European Defence Studies from MBDA
